sentences.text: Heard on I.A. No. 3020 of 2025 , which is first application under Section 430(1) of B.N.S.S., 2023 on behalf of appellant Haidar Ali for suspension of sentence and release on bail.

The appellant is aggrieved of the judgment dated 25.01.2025 passed by the learned Second Additional Sessions Judge, Waidhan, District Singrauli in S.T. No. 76/2021 whereby the appellant has been convicted under Section 323/34 of IPC and sentenced to R.I. for 6 months and fine of Rs.500/- and also under Section 376(1)/109 of IPC and sentenced to R.I. for 15 years and fine of Rs.15,000/- along with default stipulations.

entities.text: Second Additional Sessions Judge, Waidhan, District Singrauli
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: It is submitted that the appellant is innocent and has been falsely implicated in this case.
It is further submitted that as far as appellant Haidar Ali is concerned, the prosecutrix has given clean chit to him.
There is extreme delay in lodging of FIR.
The prosecutrix has admitted that there was no enmity between the two parties.
There are good chances of success of this appeal.
On these grounds, learned counsel for the appellant prays for suspension of sentence and grant of bail to the appellant.
2 CRA-1473-2025 Learned Public Prosecutor opposes the application for suspension of sentence and grant of bail to the appellant.

After hearing learned counsel for the parties and going through the record so also the fact that the appeal is going to take time for its disposal, without commenting on the merits of the case, we are of the considered opinion that this is a fit case to suspend the remaining jail sentence of the appellant Haidar Ali and to release him on bail.
Accordingly, I.A. No. 3020 of 2025 is allowed.

It is directed that on depositing the fine amount, if not already deposited and on furnishing a personal bond to the tune of Rs.30,000/- (Rupees Thirty Thousand Only) with two solvent sureties Haidar Ali vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 8 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/65287991/
